title: 1996 AHSME Problem 11
statement: Given a circle of radius \(2,\) there are many line segments of length \(2\) that are tangent to the circle at their midpoints. Find the area of the region consisting of all such line segments.

solutions.text: Each segment is centered at a tangency point \(2\) units from the circle’s center and extends \(1\) unit along the tangent in both directions. As the tangency point rotates, the segments fill the annulus with inner radius \(2\) and outer radius \(\sqrt{2^2+1^2}=\sqrt5.\) Its area is \(\pi(5-4)=\pi,\) so the correct answer is D.
hints: Each tangent segment extends one unit in each direction from its midpoint
Use a right triangle from the circle’s center to locate the inner and outer radii of the swept region
